newsitem.title: CANADA: Coastal, Westcoast to form energy megamarketer.
newsitem.headline: Coastal, Westcoast to form energy megamarketer.

text.p: Coastal Corp. and Westcoast Energy Inc. said Tuesday they plan to merge their marketing and services units to form a natural gas and electricity megamarketer.
The deal would create North America's fourth largest energy marketing company with expected annual revenues of $3 billion.
Under the agreement, which is still subject to final approval, Houston-based Coastal and Westcoast of Vancouver, British Columbia, would each hold a 50 percent stake in the new company.
The companies said the new firm would handle seven billion cubic feet of natural gas per day and become a leading wholesaler of electricity in North America.

The deal, which gained widespread analyst approval in reports leading up to the announcement, follows several recent similar moves to form so-called megamarketers, including mergers between NGC Corp. and Chevron Corp., as well as PanEnergy Corp. and Mobil Corp.
Shell Canada Ltd., one of Canada's biggest gas producers, said Monday it was joining major U.S. marketer Coral Energy, which would sell its 800 million cubic feet per day output.

Westcoast and Coastal said the merged operation would offer natural gas and electric sales and trading, multi-fuels management, energy risk management, financial services and retail product development.
As part of the deal, Westcoast will make an equalisation payment of $50 million to Coastal. An additional $10 million may also be paid, depending upon the financial performance of the new company.

Coastal, a large, integrated oil and gas firm, said the merger gives it both an expanded marketing area and economies of scale, which are often cited as reasons for the current wave of gas and electricity deals.
"Part of the equation is not just extending the marketing reach, but also (reducing) the per-unit cost," said Coastal spokesman Brian Mitchell.

Westcoast Energy, operator of British Columbia's gas pipeline system as well as gas utilities Centra and Union Gas, said it pursued the deal because it offered the size and scope not available inside its own operation.
"We had been growing it within but it's very slow and very difficult, so this is a quantum leap for us," Westcoast President Art Willms said of his firm's Westcoast Gas Services unit.

Clark Smith, president and chief executive officer of Coastal Gas Marketing Co., will assume those titles at the new company. He will report to a board on which Coastal and Westcoast will have equal representation.
The new company will maintain offices in Houston and Calgary. A corporate name was still to be developed, the companies said.
Willms said that while the decreasing number of small marketers would likely keep playing a role in the North American gas industry, the move to megamarketers was set to continue.

"Because of decreasing margins and so on, you will see significant combinations like this, and they will not only sell natural gas but, as we point out, electricity and other energy sources," Willms said. "You'll see full-service energy providers."
Coastal stock on the New York Stock Exchange closed Tuesday at $41.13, up 37.5 cents. Westcoast shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange ended up C10 cents to C$21.55 ($15.73).
